lawyer:
Afsana Begum, Advocate ------ For Petitioners. 
Md Afzal Hossain ------ For the Respondent No. 2.
parties:
Wadud Sheikh (Md) and another ------ Petitioners
vs
Artha Rin Adalat and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Respondent No. 2 Bank instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 9 of 2003 as plaintiff ("Respondent") against the present Petitioners ("Petitioners") as Defendants for realization of loan amounting to Taka 1,11,934. The said suit was decreed against the Petitioners. Thereafter the Respondent Bank as decree holder put the said decree into execution by filing Artha Jari Case No. 17 of 2004. In the said execution case the mortgaged property was placed at auction under sections 33(1) and 33(4) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 ("Ain") but no bidders participated in the auction, consequent upon which the Respondent Bank filed an application under section 33(5) of the Ain praying for issuance of a certificate in favour of the Respondent Bank vesting with the right of enjoyment and possession of the mortgaged property. The Artha Rin Adalat by its Order dated 5-4-2005 issued a certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain in favour of the Respondent Bank. The Petitioners after issuance of the certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain filed an application on 11-5-2005 for recalling the said Order dated 5-4-2005. The Artha Rin Adalat upon hearing rejected the same. Subsequently the dispute between the Respondent Bank and the petitioners, as claimed by the Petitioners, came into end by a compromise and on the basis of said compromise the Petitioners have already made payment of all the dues to the Bank. But the Bank decree holder most illegally filed Second Execution Case being Artha Jari Case No. 111 of 2005 against the Petitioners on 21-11-2005 and on the very day of filing this Second Execution Case the Artha Rin Adalat issued warrant of arrest to the Petitioner on the prayer of the decree holder Bank. 

 4. The Respondent Bank contested the Rule by filing Affidavit-in-opposition, Supplementary affidavit-in-opposition denying all the material allegations made by the Petitioners in the application contending, inter alia, that the certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain issued by the Artha Rin Adalat is legal and valid and the decree holder Bank rightly initiated Second Execution proceeding against the Petitioners and the Artha Rin Adalat legally issued warrant of arrest. 

 5. Mrs Afsana Begum, the learned advocate appearing for the Petitioners submits that the instant Second Execution Case is not maintainable in law because of the fact that the First Execution Case No. 17 of 2004 is still pending and during pendency of the First Execution Case the law does not permit the decree holder to initiate Second Execution Case against the Petitioners. She further submits that admittedly a certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain has been issued by the Court in favour of the decree holder Bank with the right of possession and enjoyment of the property till realization of the decretal amount from the Petitioners. Referring section 33(5) of the Ain she also argued that the law says after obtaining certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain the decree holder Bank ought to have sold the property by auction and adjust the sale proceeds with the decretal amount and in the event of any short fall the decree holder can initiate Second Execution proceeding against the Petitioner-judgment debtors. But in the instant case after obtaining certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain the Bank took no steps for selling the property as per the provision contained in section 33(5) of the Ain. Without selling the property by auction second execution case cannot be filed and, as such, issuance of warrant of arrest against the petitioners by the impugned Order is also palpably illegal on the face of it. 

 6. Referring section 30 of the Ain, she further submits that after filing of the Second Execution Case, it was incumbent upon the decree holder and the Court to serve notice upon the Judgment-debtor through Process Server as well as through Post Office registered with AD. But the impugned Order shows that no notice as required by law was issued and served upon the Judgment-debtor-Petitioners. Without issuance and service of the notice of filing of the Second Execution Case issuance of warrant of arrest at the instance of the decree holder is illegal and without lawful authority. 

 11. Therefore, during pendency of an Execution Case, the law does not permit the decree holder to initiate a further execution case against the Judgment debtor as per provision of section 33(6) of the Ain. Furthermore, it is incumbent upon the Bank decree holder to sell the property by auction and adjust the sale proceeds with the decretal amount and in the event of any shortfall, the decree holder Bank can proceed with the Second Execution Case as per sub-section (6) of section 33 of the Ain. But in the instant case, the provision of Sub-sections (5) and (6) of section 33 of the Ain has not been complied with by the Respondent Bank. Furthermore, without compliance of the provision of sub-section (5) and (6) of section 33 of the Ain as it appears from the instant case, the decree holder Bank most unfortunately initiated the Second Execution Case against the Petitioner and very interestingly, the Artha Rin Adalat, on the very day of filing Second Execution Case without issuing any notice for service upon the Judgment-debtors violating the provisions of law as well as principle of natural justice as endorsed by our Appellate Division directly issued warrant of arrest against the present Petitioners. 

 14. From a perusal of the above quoted sections of the Ain, this Court finds that in every proceeding under this law, issuance of notice for service upon the defendant or opposite party is mandatory under section 30(1) of the Ain and in the event of issuance of a certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain vesting the right of possession and enjoyment with the decree holder, it is incumbent upon the certificate holder to sell the property by auction and to adjust the sale proceeds with the decretal amount and in the event of any shortfall the decree holder can proceed with the Second Execution Case for realization of the remaining claim, as provided in section 33(6) of the Ain. 

 15. In the instant case, this Court finds that the decree holder Bank as well as the Artha Rin Adalat, in violation of the said provisions of law, proceeded with the Second Execution Case and issued warrant of arrest without issuance of any notice to the Petitioner. The Learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat in this Court's considered view (and being aware of the propriety in not casting aspersion) has failed to show that he has rudimentary knowledge about the laws in general and the Artha Rin Adalat Ain in particular. Resultantly, the impugned Order as well as the proceeding in Artha Jari Case No. 111 of 2005 is found to be illegal and absolutely contrary to the provisions of law. 

 a) In the event of failure of the Certificate holder in selling the property at an appropriate price by auction in that case by deducting the determined price of the property or a reasonable price the decree holder can file further execution case subject to the provision of section 28 of the Ain. 

 b) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law the decree holder may apply before the court within 6 years praying for a certificate of title under section 33(7) of the Ain and in the absence of such application with the expiry of 6 years the title of the property shall automatically vest in the decree holder and a certificate to that effect can be obtained from the court by the decree holder.
